feature.name: Second Wind
feature.description: As a Bonus Action, you can regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level. You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. Uses: 2 (levels 1-3), 3 (levels 4-9), 4 (levels 10-20).

feature.name: Action Surge
feature.description: On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

feature.name: Tactical Mind
feature.description: When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature.name: Tactical Shift
feature.description: Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a Bonus Action, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

feature.name: Indomitable
feature.description: If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest. You can use this feature twice before a Long Rest starting at level 13 and three times before a Long Rest starting at level 17.

feature.name: Tactical Master
feature.description: When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Push, Sap, or Slow property for that attack.

feature.name: Two Extra Attacks
feature.description: You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature.name: Studied Attacks
feature.description: If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

feature.name: Three Extra Attacks
feature.description: You can attack four times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.description: You know Wizard cantrips and keep a spellbook of level 1+ Wizard spells. Each day you prepare spells from your spellbook (see the Prepared Spells column); you can change the list when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips with another Wizard cantrip. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus.

feature.name: Ritual Adept
feature.description: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

feature.name: Arcane Recovery
feature.description: When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Memorize Spell
feature.description: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

feature.name: Spell Mastery
feature.description: Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of those spells with an eligible spell of the same level from the book.

feature.name: Signature Spells
feature.description: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't cast them in this way again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

feature.name: Rage
feature.description: You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren't wearing Heavy armor. Uses: 2 (levels 1-2), 3 (3-5), 4 (6-11), 5 (12-16), 6 (17-20); you regain one expended use on a Short Rest and all on a Long Rest. While active: Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; Rage Damage bonus when you attack using Strength (+2 at levels 1-8, +3 at 9-15, +4 at 16-20); Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws; you can't maintain Concentration or cast spells. The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn and can be extended each round, up to 10 minutes; it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition.

feature.name: Unarmored Defense
feature.description: While you aren't wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

feature.name: Weapon Mastery
feature.description: You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change one of those weapon choices. You gain more kinds at Barbarian levels 4 (3) and 10 (4).

feature.name: Danger Sense
feature.description: You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

feature.name: Reckless Attack
feature.description: When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time.

feature.name: Primal Knowledge
feature.description: You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1. In addition, while your Rage is active, whenever you make an ability check using Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival, you can make it as a Strength check.

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature.name: Fast Movement
feature.description: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

feature.name: Feral Instinct
feature.description: You have Advantage on Initiative rolls.

feature.name: Instinctive Pounce
feature.description: As part of the Bonus Action you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your Speed.

feature.name: Brutal Strike
feature.description: If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have Disadvantage. If it hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the same type, and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect: Forceful Blow (the target is pushed 15 feet straight away from you; you can then move up to half your Speed straight toward it without provoking Opportunity Attacks) or Hamstring Blow (the target's Speed is reduced by 15 feet until the start of your next turn).

feature.name: Relentless Rage
feature.description: If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your Hit Points instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level. Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, the DC resets to 10.

feature.name: Improved Brutal Strike
feature.description: New Brutal Strike options: Staggering Blow (the target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes, and it can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn) and Sundering Blow (before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by another creature against the target gains a +5 bonus).

feature.name: Persistent Rage
feature.description: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended uses of Rage; once you do so, you can't again until you finish a Long Rest. Your Rage now lasts for 10 minutes without needing to be extended; it ends early if you have the Unconscious condition or don Heavy armor.

effects.note: Pode recuperar todos os usos de Rage gastos (uma vez por Descanso Longo).

feature.name: Improved Brutal Strike
feature.description: The extra damage of your Brutal Strike increases to 2d10, and you can use two different Brutal Strike effects whenever you use it.

feature.name: Indomitable Might
feature.description: If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

feature.name: Primal Champion
feature.description: Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

feature.name: Bardic Inspiration
feature.description: As a Bonus Action, you can inspire another creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice (a d6; d8 at level 5, d10 at level 10, d12 at level 15). A creature can have only one at a time. Once within the next hour when the creature fails a D20 Test, it can roll the die and add the number rolled to the d20. You can confer it a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.description: You cast Bard spells using Charisma. You know two Bard cantrips (one more at levels 4 and 10); whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one cantrip. You prepare level 1+ Bard spells as shown in the Prepared Spells column; whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one prepared spell with another Bard spell for which you have spell slots. You can use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus.

feature.name: Expertise
feature.description: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

feature.name: Jack of All Trades
feature.description: You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your Proficiency Bonus.

feature.name: Font of Inspiration
feature.description: You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest. In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.

feature.name: Countercharm
feature.description: If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has Advantage.

feature.name: Magical Secrets
feature.description: Whenever you reach a Bard level (including this level) and the Prepared Spells number increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, and Wizard spell lists, and the chosen spells count as Bard spells for you. In addition, whenever you replace a spell prepared for this class, you can replace it with a spell from those lists.

feature.name: Superior Inspiration
feature.description: When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.

effects.note: Recupera usos de Bardic Inspiration até ter 2, se tiver menos.

feature.name: Words of Creation
feature.description: You always have the Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill spells prepared. When you cast either spell, you can target a second creature with it if that creature is within 10 feet of the first target.

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.description: You cast Cleric spells using Wisdom. You know three Cleric cantrips (one more at levels 4 and 10); whenever you gain a Cleric level, you can replace one cantrip. You prepare level 1+ Cleric spells as shown in the Prepared Spells column, and you can change the list whenever you finish a Long Rest. You can use a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus.

feature.name: Divine Order
feature.description: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice: Protector (proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor) or Thaumaturge (one extra Cleric cantrip and a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum of +1).

feature.name: Channel Divinity
feature.description: You can channel divine energy to create one of this class's Channel Divinity effects. Uses: 2 (levels 2-5), 3 (6-17), 4 (18-20); you regain one expended use on a Short Rest and all on a Long Rest. Save DC equals your Cleric spell save DC. Divine Spark: as a Magic action, roll 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier (2d8 at level 7, 3d8 at 13, 4d8 at 18) and either restore that many Hit Points to a creature within 30 feet or force it to make a Constitution saving throw, taking Necrotic or Radiant damage on a failure (half on a success). Turn Undead: as a Magic action, each Undead of your choice within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions for 1 minute, ending early if it takes damage.

feature.name: Sear Undead
feature.description: Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8) and add the rolls together. Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll's total. This damage doesn't end the turn effect.

feature.name: Blessed Strikes
feature.description: You gain one of the following options of your choice: Divine Strike (once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, the target takes an extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage) or Potent Spellcasting (add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip).

feature.name: Improved Blessed Strikes (Divine Strike)
feature.description: The extra damage of your Divine Strike increases to 2d8.

feature.name: Improved Blessed Strikes (Potent Spellcasting)
feature.description: When you cast a Cleric cantrip and deal damage to a creature with it, you can give vitality to yourself or another creature within 60 feet of yourself, granting a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier.

feature.name: Divine Intervention
feature.description: As a Magic action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a Reaction to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. You can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Greater Divine Intervention
feature.description: When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose Wish when you select a spell. If you do so, you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish 2d4 Long Rests.

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.description: You cast Druid spells using Wisdom. You know two Druid cantrips (one more at levels 4 and 10); whenever you gain a Druid level, you can replace one cantrip. You prepare level 1+ Druid spells as shown in the Prepared Spells column, and you can change the list whenever you finish a Long Rest. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus.

feature.name: Druidic
feature.description: You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids, and you always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared. You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages; others spot such a message with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check but can't decipher it without magic.

feature.name: Primal Order
feature.description: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice: Magician (one extra Druid cantrip and a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum of +1) or Warden (proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor).

feature.name: Wild Shape
feature.description: As a Bonus Action, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned. You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die; you can leave early as a Bonus Action. Uses: 2 (levels 2-5), 3 (6-16), 4 (17-20); you regain one on a Short Rest and all on a Long Rest. Known forms: 4 Beasts of CR 1/4 without Fly Speed (6 of CR 1/2 at level 4; 8 of CR 1 at level 8, which may have a Fly Speed). While shape-shifted you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Druid level, use the Beast's statistics but keep your creature type, Hit Points, Hit Point Dice, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma, class features, languages, feats, and proficiencies, and you can't cast spells.

feature.name: Wild Companion
feature.description: As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the Find Familiar spell without Material components. When you cast the spell in this way, the familiar is Fey and disappears when you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Wild Resurgence
feature.description: Once on each of your turns, if you have no uses of Wild Shape left, you can give yourself one use by expending a spell slot (no action required). In addition, you can expend one use of Wild Shape (no action required) to give yourself a level 1 spell slot, but you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Elemental Fury
feature.description: You gain one of the following options of your choice: Potent Spellcasting (add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Druid cantrip) or Primal Strike (once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or a Beast form's attack in Wild Shape, the target takes an extra 1d8 Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage).

feature.name: Improved Elemental Fury (Potent Spellcasting)
feature.description: When you cast a Druid cantrip with a range of 10 feet or greater, the spell's range increases by 300 feet.

feature.name: Improved Elemental Fury (Primal Strike)
feature.description: The extra damage of your Primal Strike increases to 2d8.

feature.name: Beast Spells
feature.description: While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component.

feature.name: Archdruid
feature.description: Evergreen Wild Shape: whenever you roll Initiative and have no uses of Wild Shape left, you regain one expended use of it. Nature Magician: you can convert uses of Wild Shape into a single spell slot (each use contributes 2 spell levels); once per Long Rest. Longevity: for every ten years that pass, your body ages only one year.

effects.note: Evergreen Wild Shape: sem usos de Wild Shape, recupera 1.

feature.name: Martial Arts
feature.description: Your Monk weapons are Simple Melee weapons and Martial Melee weapons that have the Light property. While you are unarmed or wielding only Monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield: you can make an Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action; you can roll your Martial Arts die (1d6; 1d8 at level 5, 1d10 at 11, 1d12 at 17) in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strike or Monk weapons; and you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons (and for the save DC of Grapple or Shove).

feature.name: Unarmored Defense
feature.description: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.

feature.name: Monk's Focus
feature.description: You have a number of Focus Points equal to your Monk level, regained on a Short or Long Rest. Save DC for Monk features: 8 + Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus. Flurry of Blows: expend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action. Patient Defense: take the Disengage action as a Bonus Action, or expend 1 Focus Point to take both Disengage and Dodge. Step of the Wind: take the Dash action as a Bonus Action, or expend 1 Focus Point to take both Disengage and Dash, with your jump distance doubled for the turn.

feature.name: Unarmored Movement
feature.description: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield. This bonus increases at Monk levels 6 (+15 ft.), 10 (+20 ft.), 14 (+25 ft.), and 18 (+30 ft.).

feature.name: Uncanny Metabolism
feature.description: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your Martial Arts die, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

effects.note: Pode recuperar todos os Focus Points gastos e PV iguais ao nível de Monge + o dado de Martial Arts (uma vez por Descanso Longo).

feature.name: Deflect Attacks
feature.description: When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the attack's total damage against you by 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier and Monk level. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect some of the attack's force: a creature within 5 feet (melee) or 60 feet (ranged) must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die plus your Dexterity modifier.

feature.name: Slow Fall
feature.description: You can take a Reaction when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature.name: Stunning Strike
feature.description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target's Speed is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against the target before then has Advantage.

feature.name: Empowered Strikes
feature.description: Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

feature.name: Unarmored Movement
feature.description: Your Unarmored Movement bonus increases by 5 feet.

feature.name: Evasion
feature.description: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You don't benefit from this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

feature.name: Acrobatic Movement
feature.description: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.

feature.name: Heightened Focus
feature.description: Flurry of Blows: you can expend 1 Focus Point to make three Unarmed Strikes instead of two. Patient Defense: when you expend a Focus Point to use it, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die. Step of the Wind: when you expend a Focus Point to use it, you can move a willing Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of yourself with you until the end of your turn, without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

feature.name: Self-Restoration
feature.description: You can remove one of the following conditions from yourself at the end of each of your turns: Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned. In addition, forgoing food and drink doesn't give you levels of Exhaustion.

effects.note: Pode encerrar em você Enfeitiçado, Amedrontado ou Envenenado (uma delas).

feature.name: Unarmored Movement
feature.description: Your Unarmored Movement bonus increases by 5 feet.

feature.name: Deflect Energy
feature.description: You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

feature.name: Disciplined Survivor
feature.description: You gain proficiency in all saving throws. Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.

feature.name: Unarmored Movement
feature.description: Your Unarmored Movement bonus increases by 5 feet.

feature.name: Perfect Focus
feature.description: When you roll Initiative and don't use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.

effects.note: Sem usar Uncanny Metabolism, recupera Focus Points até ter 4, se tiver 3 ou menos.

feature.name: Superior Defense
feature.description: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. During that time, you have Resistance to all damage except Force damage.

feature.name: Unarmored Movement
feature.description: Your Unarmored Movement bonus increases by 5 feet.

feature.name: Body and Mind
feature.description: Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

feature.name: Lay On Hands
feature.description: You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a Long Rest, with which you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Paladin level. As a Bonus Action, you can touch a creature (which could be yourself) and draw power from the pool to restore Hit Points to it, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool. You can also expend 5 Hit Points from the pool to remove the Poisoned condition from the creature.

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.description: You cast Paladin spells using Charisma. You prepare level 1+ Paladin spells as shown in the Prepared Spells column; whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Paladin spell for which you have spell slots. You can use a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus.

feature.name: Weapon Mastery
feature.description: You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

feature.name: Fighting Style
feature.description: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose Blessed Warrior: you learn two Cleric cantrips of your choice, which count as Paladin spells for you, with Charisma as your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Paladin level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Cleric cantrip.

options.name: Blessed Warrior
options.description: Two Cleric cantrips; Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them.

feature.name: Paladin's Smite
feature.description: You always have the Divine Smite spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

feature.name: Channel Divinity
feature.description: You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice (three times from Paladin level 11). You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest and all on a Long Rest. Save DCs equal your Paladin spell save DC. Divine Sense: as a Bonus Action, for 10 minutes or until you have the Incapacitated condition, you know the location and type of any Celestial, Fiend, or Undead within 60 feet of yourself, and you detect consecrated or desecrated places and objects in that radius.

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature.name: Faithful Steed
feature.description: You always have the Find Steed spell prepared. You can also cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Aura of Protection
feature.description: You radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot Emanation that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition. You and your allies in the aura gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum bonus of +1). A creature can benefit from only one Aura of Protection at a time.

feature.name: Abjure Foes
feature.description: As a Magic action, you can expend one use of this class's Channel Divinity to target a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. While Frightened in this way, a target can do only one of the following on its turns: move, take an action, or take a Bonus Action.

feature.name: Aura of Courage
feature.description: You and your allies have Immunity to the Frightened condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Frightened ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

feature.name: Radiant Strikes
feature.description: When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, the target takes an extra 1d8 Radiant damage.

feature.name: Restoring Touch
feature.description: When you use Lay On Hands on a creature, you can also remove one or more of the following conditions from the creature: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned. You must expend 5 Hit Points from the healing pool for each condition you remove; those points don't also restore Hit Points.

feature.name: Aura Expansion
feature.description: Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot Emanation.

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.description: You cast Ranger spells using Wisdom. You prepare level 1+ Ranger spells as shown in the Prepared Spells column; whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Ranger spell for which you have spell slots. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus.

feature.name: Favored Enemy
feature.description: You always have the Hunter's Mark spell prepared. You can cast it without expending a spell slot a number of times shown in the Favored Enemy column (2 at level 1, 3 at 5, 4 at 9, 5 at 13, 6 at 17), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Weapon Mastery
feature.description: You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

feature.name: Deft Explorer
feature.description: Expertise: choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise; you gain Expertise in that skill. Languages: you know two languages of your choice from the language tables in Character Creation.

feature.name: Fighting Style
feature.description: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose Druidic Warrior: you learn two Druid cantrips of your choice, which count as Ranger spells for you, with Wisdom as your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Ranger level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Druid cantrip.

options.name: Druidic Warrior
options.description: Two Druid cantrips; Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them.

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature.name: Roving
feature.description: Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor. You also have a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

feature.name: Tireless
feature.description: As a Magic action, you can give yourself Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1), a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once) per Long Rest. Whenever you finish a Short Rest, your Exhaustion level, if any, decreases by 1.

feature.name: Relentless Hunter
feature.description: Taking damage can't break your Concentration on Hunter's Mark.

feature.name: Nature's Veil
feature.description: As a Bonus Action, you can give yourself the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Precise Hunter
feature.description: You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.

feature.name: Feral Senses
feature.description: You have Blindsight with a range of 30 feet.

feature.name: Foe Slayer
feature.description: The damage die of your Hunter's Mark is a d10 rather than a d6.

feature.name: Expertise
feature.description: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. At Rogue level 6, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

feature.name: Sneak Attack
feature.description: Once per turn, you can deal extra damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. You don't need Advantage if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition, and you don't have Disadvantage on the attack roll. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type. Sneak Attack: 1d6 at level 1, increasing by 1d6 every odd Rogue level (2d6 at 3, 3d6 at 5 ... 10d6 at 19).

feature.name: Thieves' Cant
feature.description: You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in Character Creation.

feature.name: Weapon Mastery
feature.description: You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

feature.name: Cunning Action
feature.description: On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a Bonus Action: Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

feature.name: Steady Aim
feature.description: As a Bonus Action, you give yourself Advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your Speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.

feature.name: Cunning Strike
feature.description: When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one Cunning Strike effect by forgoing Sneak Attack dice (save DC 8 + Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus): Poison (1d6; requires a Poisoner's Kit; Constitution save or Poisoned for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each turn), Trip (1d6; a Large or smaller target makes a Dexterity save or has the Prone condition), Withdraw (1d6; immediately after the attack, move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks).

feature.name: Uncanny Dodge
feature.description: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

feature.name: Evasion
feature.description: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

feature.name: Reliable Talent
feature.description: Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

feature.name: Improved Cunning Strike
feature.description: You can use up to two Cunning Strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

feature.name: Devious Strikes
feature.description: New Cunning Strike options: Daze (2d6; Constitution save or on its next turn it can do only one of move, action, or Bonus Action), Knock Out (6d6; Constitution save or Unconscious for 1 minute or until it takes damage, repeating the save at the end of each turn), Obscure (3d6; Dexterity save or Blinded until the end of its next turn).

feature.name: Slippery Mind
feature.description: You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

feature.name: Elusive
feature.description: No attack roll can have Advantage against you unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

feature.name: Stroke of Luck
feature.description: If you fail a D20 Test, you can turn the roll into a 20. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.description: You cast Sorcerer spells using Charisma. You know four Sorcerer cantrips (one more at levels 4 and 10); whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one cantrip. You prepare level 1+ Sorcerer spells as shown in the Prepared Spells column; whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus.

feature.name: Innate Sorcery
feature.description: As a Bonus Action, you can unleash your innate magic for 1 minute, during which the spell save DC of your Sorcerer spells increases by 1 and you have Advantage on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Font of Magic
feature.description: You have Sorcery Points equal to your Sorcerer level (from level 2), regained on a Long Rest. You can expend a spell slot to gain Sorcery Points equal to the slot's level (no action required). As a Bonus Action, you can transform Sorcery Points into one spell slot of level 5 or lower: level 1 costs 2 points (Sorcerer level 2), level 2 costs 3 (level 3), level 3 costs 5 (level 5), level 4 costs 6 (level 7), level 5 costs 7 (level 9). Created slots vanish when you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Metamagic
feature.description: You gain two Metamagic options of your choice, and two more at Sorcerer levels 10 and 17. To use an option, you spend the Sorcery Points it costs; you can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it unless otherwise noted. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don't know.

feature.name: Careful Spell
feature.description: Cost: 1 Sorcery Point. When you cast a spell that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell, and it takes no damage if it would normally take half damage on a successful save.

feature.name: Distant Spell
feature.description: Cost: 1 Sorcery Point. When you cast a spell that has a range of at least 5 feet, you can double the spell's range. Or when you cast a spell that has a range of Touch, you can make the spell's range 30 feet.

feature.name: Empowered Spell
feature.description: Cost: 1 Sorcery Point. When you roll damage for a spell, you can reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one), and you must use the new rolls. You can use Empowered Spell even if you've already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

feature.name: Extended Spell
feature.description: Cost: 1 Sorcery Point. When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can double its duration to a maximum duration of 24 hours. If the affected spell requires Concentration, you have Advantage on any saving throw you make to maintain that Concentration.

feature.name: Heightened Spell
feature.description: Cost: 2 Sorcery Points. When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can give one target of the spell Disadvantage on saves against the spell.

feature.name: Quickened Spell
feature.description: Cost: 2 Sorcery Points. When you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can change the casting time to a Bonus Action for this casting. You can't modify a spell in this way if you've already cast a level 1+ spell on the current turn, nor can you cast a level 1+ spell on this turn after modifying a spell in this way.

feature.name: Seeking Spell
feature.description: Cost: 1 Sorcery Point. If you make an attack roll for a spell and miss, you can reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll. You can use Seeking Spell even if you've already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

feature.name: Subtle Spell
feature.description: Cost: 1 Sorcery Point. When you cast a spell, you can cast it without any Verbal, Somatic, or Material components, except Material components that are consumed by the spell or that have a cost specified in the spell.

feature.name: Transmuted Spell
feature.description: Cost: 1 Sorcery Point. When you cast a spell that deals Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage, you can change that damage type to one of the other listed types.

feature.name: Twinned Spell
feature.description: Cost: 1 Sorcery Point. When you cast a spell, such as Charm Person, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot to target an additional creature, you can increase the spell's effective level by 1.

feature.name: Sorcerous Restoration
feature.description: When you finish a Short Rest, you can regain expended Sorcery Points, but no more than a number equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Sorcery Incarnate
feature.description: If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can use it if you spend 2 Sorcery Points when you take the Bonus Action to activate it. In addition, while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use up to two of your Metamagic options on each spell you cast.

feature.description: While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on it.

feature.name: Eldritch Invocations
feature.description: You gain one invocation of your choice, and more as shown in the Invocations column (3 at level 2, 5 at 5, 6 at 7, 7 at 9, 8 at 12, 9 at 15, 10 at 18). If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify; you can't replace an invocation that is a prerequisite for another one you have. You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

feature.name: Agonizing Blast
feature.description: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage. You can add your Charisma modifier to that spell's damage rolls. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time. Prerequisite: a Warlock cantrip that deals damage (checked by the GM).

feature.name: Armor of Shadows
feature.description: You can cast Mage Armor on yourself without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Ascendant Step
feature.description: You can cast Levitate on yourself without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Devil's Sight
feature.description: You can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness, both magical and nonmagical, within 120 feet of yourself.

feature.name: Devouring Blade
feature.description: The Extra Attack of your Thirsting Blade invocation confers two extra attacks rather than one.

feature.name: Eldritch Mind
feature.description: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain Concentration.

feature.name: Eldritch Smite
feature.description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra 1d8 Force damage to the target, plus another 1d8 per level of the spell slot, and you can give the target the Prone condition if it is Huge or smaller.

feature.name: Eldritch Spear
feature.description: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage and has a range of 10+ feet. When you cast that spell, its range increases by a number of feet equal to 30 times your Warlock level. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time. Prerequisite: a Warlock cantrip that deals damage (checked by the GM).

feature.name: Fiendish Vigor
feature.description: You can cast False Life on yourself without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell with this feature, you don't roll the die for the Temporary Hit Points; you automatically get the highest number on the die.

feature.name: Gaze of Two Minds
feature.description: You can use a Bonus Action to touch a willing creature and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn, maintaining the connection with a Bonus Action on subsequent turns. While perceiving through the other creature's senses, you benefit from any special senses it has, and you can cast spells as if you were in your space or its space if the two of you are within 60 feet of each other.

feature.name: Gift of the Depths
feature.description: You can breathe underwater, and you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed. You can also cast Water Breathing once without expending a spell slot, regaining the ability on a Long Rest.

feature.name: Gift of the Protectors
feature.description: A new page appears in your Book of Shadows, which can contain a number of names equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). When any creature whose name is on the page is reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, the creature magically drops to 1 Hit Point instead. Once this magic is triggered, no creature can benefit from it until you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Investment of the Chain Master
feature.description: When you cast Find Familiar, the familiar gains a Fly Speed or a Swim Speed of 40 feet; as a Bonus Action, you can command it to take the Attack action; it can deal Necrotic or Radiant damage instead of Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing; it uses your spell save DC; and when it takes damage, you can take a Reaction to grant it Resistance against that damage.

feature.name: Lessons of the First Ones
feature.description: You gain one Origin feat of your choice. Repeatable: choose a different Origin feat each time.

feature.name: Lifedrinker
feature.description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage (your choice), and you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice to roll it and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point).

feature.name: Mask of Many Faces
feature.description: You can cast Disguise Self without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Master of Myriad Forms
feature.description: You can cast Alter Self without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Misty Visions
feature.description: You can cast Silent Image without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: One with Shadows
feature.description: While you're in an area of Dim Light or Darkness, you can cast Invisibility on yourself without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Otherworldly Leap
feature.description: You can cast Jump on yourself without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Pact of the Blade
feature.description: As a Bonus Action, you can conjure a pact weapon in your hand (a Simple or Martial Melee weapon of your choice with which you bond) or create a bond with a magic weapon you touch. Until the bond ends, you have proficiency with the weapon and can use it as a Spellcasting Focus. Whenever you attack with the bonded weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of Strength or Dexterity, and you can cause it to deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage or its normal type. The bond ends if you use this Bonus Action again, if the weapon is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more, or if you die.

feature.description: You learn the Find Familiar spell and can cast it as a Magic action without expending a spell slot. You can choose a special form for your familiar: Imp, Pseudodragon, Quasit, Skeleton, Sphinx of Wonder, Sprite, or Venomous Snake. When you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its Reaction.

feature.name: Pact of the Tome
feature.description: At the end of a Short or Long Rest, you conjure a Book of Shadows. Choose three cantrips and two level 1 spells that have the Ritual tag, from any class's spell list, that you don't already have prepared. While the book is on your person, you have the chosen spells prepared, and they function as Warlock spells for you. You can use the book as a Spellcasting Focus.

When you hit a Large or smaller creature with that cantrip, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from you. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time. Prerequisite: a Warlock cantrip that deals damage (checked by the GM).

feature.name: Witch Sight

feature.name: Lessons of the First Ones

feature.description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage (your choice), and you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice to roll it and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point).

feature.name: Mask of Many Faces
feature.description: You can cast Disguise Self without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Master of Myriad Forms
feature.description: You can cast Alter Self without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Misty Visions
feature.description: You can cast Silent Image without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: One with Shadows
feature.description: While you're in an area of Dim Light or Darkness, you can cast Invisibility on yourself without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Otherworldly Leap
feature.description: You can cast Jump on yourself without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Pact of the Blade
feature.description: As a Bonus Action, you can conjure a pact weapon in your hand (a Simple or Martial Melee weapon of your choice with which you bond) or create a bond with a magic weapon you touch. Until the bond ends, you have proficiency with the weapon and can use it as a Spellcasting Focus. Whenever you attack with the bonded weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of Strength or Dexterity, and you can cause it to deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage or its normal type. The bond ends if you use this Bonus Action again, if the weapon is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more, or if you die.

feature.name: Pact of the Chain
feature.description: You learn the Find Familiar spell and can cast it as a Magic action without expending a spell slot. You can choose a special form for your familiar: Imp, Pseudodragon, Quasit, Skeleton, Sphinx of Wonder, Sprite, or Venomous Snake. When you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its Reaction.

feature.name: Pact of the Tome
feature.description: At the end of a Short or Long Rest, you conjure a Book of Shadows. Choose three cantrips and two level 1 spells that have the Ritual tag, from any class's spell list, that you don't already have prepared. While the book is on your person, you have the chosen spells prepared, and they function as Warlock spells for you. You can use the book as a Spellcasting Focus.

feature.name: Repelling Blast
feature.description: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that requires an attack roll. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with that cantrip, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from you. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time. Prerequisite: a Warlock cantrip that deals damage (checked by the GM).

feature.name: Thirsting Blade
feature.description: You gain the Extra Attack feature for your pact weapon only: you can attack twice with the weapon instead of once when you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature.name: Visions of Distant Realms
feature.description: You can cast Arcane Eye without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Whispers of the Grave
feature.description: You can cast Speak with Dead without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Witch Sight
feature.description: You have Truesight with a range of 30 feet.

feature.name: Agonizing Blast
feature.description: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage. You can add your Charisma modifier to that spell's damage rolls. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time. Prerequisite: a Warlock cantrip that deals damage (checked by the GM).

feature.name: Armor of Shadows
feature.description: You can cast Mage Armor on yourself without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Ascendant Step
feature.description: You can cast Levitate on yourself without expending a spell slot.

feature.name: Devil's Sight
feature.description: You can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness, both magical and nonmagical, within 120 feet of yourself.

feature.name: Devouring Blade
feature.description: The Extra Attack of your Thirsting Blade invocation confers two extra attacks rather than one.

feature.name: Eldritch Mind
feature.description: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain Concentration.

feature.name: Eldritch Smite
feature.description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra 1d8 Force damage to the target, plus another 1d8 per level of the spell slot, and you can give the target the Prone condition if it is Huge or smaller.

feature.name: Eldritch Spear
feature.description: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage and has a range of 10+ feet. When you cast that spell, its range increases by a number of feet equal to 30 times your Warlock level. Repeatable: choose a different eligible cantrip each time. Prerequisite: a Warlock cantrip that deals damage (checked by the GM).

feature.name: Fiendish Vigor
feature.description: You can cast False Life on yourself without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell with this feature, you don't roll the die for the Temporary Hit Points; you automatically get the highest number on the die.

feature.name: Gaze of Two Minds
feature.description: You can use a Bonus Action to touch a willing creature and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn, maintaining the connection with a Bonus Action on subsequent turns. While perceiving through the other creature's senses, you benefit from any special senses it has, and you can cast spells as if you were in your space or its space if the two of you are within 60 feet of each other.

feature.name: Gift of the Depths
feature.description: You can breathe underwater, and you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed. You can also cast Water Breathing once without expending a spell slot, regaining the ability on a Long Rest.

feature.name: Gift of the Protectors
feature.description: A new page appears in your Book of Shadows, which can contain a number of names equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). When any creature whose name is on the page is reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, the creature magically drops to 1 Hit Point instead. Once this magic is triggered, no creature can benefit from it until you finish a Long Rest.

feature.name: Investment of the Chain Master
